__doc__: Event registry for .workframe/state/events.jsonl. Single source of truth for event type names, reliability tiers, producers, and consumers. Workframe-private — not a Claude Code official file. TS FORMAT (binding on every producer): UTC with second precision — datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec='seconds'), e.g. 2026-08-16T07:24:04+00:00. Consumers sort and window-filter events by raw string comparison, so a single file must not mix timezones or precisions; on 2026-08-16 four variants coexisted (local/UTC x sec/microsec) with the same event type appearing in three of them, which silently mis-orders anything compared as text.

reliability_tiers.hook_deterministic: Produced by Python hook scripts (SessionStart / Stop / SubagentStop / SessionEnd). Capture is guaranteed by the Claude Code runtime as long as the hook is registered and not externally killed. Safe to use as core triggering logic and state transitions.
reliability_tiers.protocol_expected: Produced by an explicit agent-facing protocol instruction in an injected discipline shard — for example the event-stream step of the common protocol shard, or the correction handling in the main-session signal-intake shard. Useful signal but NOT guaranteed: the model may skip the write (under context pressure), duplicate it (re-running the protocol), or misattribute it. Use as corroborating signal, not single-source-of-truth.
reliability_tiers.model_mediated: Produced by a skill body or an agent reasoning step (no protocol-level enforcement). Capture depends entirely on Claude following the relevant SKILL.md instruction. Use only for audit / corroboration; do NOT base core triggering logic on these counts.
reliability_tiers.removed_v0_2_1: Event name was defined in v0.2.0 but cannot be reliably captured (e.g., rules have no trigger callback). Removed from producers and triggering logic; schema stub retained only for historical compatibility.

harness_field: OPTIONAL field on every event line: harness = cc | codex | unknown, i.e. which door produced the line. ABSENT means a legacy line written before v3; consumers read it as cc. The value unknown is written EXPLICITLY when the producer was not told which door it runs in — never omit the field to mean that, because omission already means cc. Hook producers get the value from the --harness <door> argument that the hook table puts on every command (each door has its own table, and each table writes its own door): a command-line argument, NOT environment detection — CLAUDE_* leaks into a nested `codex exec` and would make detection confidently wrong. Model-hand-written events get it from the workframe-event bin command. Single stamping point in code: _state_io.event_json(). PARTITION (binding from v3, and the reason bin entries do NOT guess `cc`): every line written BY CODE carries the field — held by routing every event-line serialization through _state_io.event_json(), which the event_line_serialization_single_source check pins at the call sites. THE BOUNDARY ON THAT WORD 'every', stated so consumers can size the claim: that check reads the append_line/append_lines call site, so a JSON string built into a variable first and only then passed in would slip past it (today zero such sites; the check's >=9 floor on event_json call sites would still catch the single-source path being abandoned wholesale, but not one producer sneaking around it). The spill / merge-back path is NOT a second channel: _spill() and merge_spills() move already-serialized whole lines and construct none of their own — verified as the general property, NOT as a list of shapes: neither function BUILDS ANY MAPPING (no dict literal, dict() call, or dict comprehension), CALLS json AT ALL (so nothing is dumped, and nothing is loaded-then-rewritten), or EMITS ANY JSON TEXT (no string literal or f-string carrying braces; their f-strings build filenames, a glob, a timestamp format and two [warn] lines). Re-check it as that property. Checking only for json.dumps and event-shaped dict literals would still report zero the day someone adds a dict(...) — the criterion has to outlive the conclusion — hook producers get cc/codex from their command line; bin entries (workframe-event, workframe-recompute-board-summary, workframe-recompute-skill-metrics; they all accept --harness, pass it when you know the door) — and that parenthesis is THE list: anything that tells a model to pass --harness must point here rather than retype the names, because a second copy silently misses the fourth event-writing entry the day one appears. Passing it to a bin entry that is NOT on this list is not harmless: workframe-doctor and workframe-module-close-check parse args and exit 2 on an unknown one, and BOTH already use a non-zero exit to mean 'I found problems', so the argument error and a real finding look identical in the terminal — the reader goes looking at the project instead of at the argument. Those three listed entries write `unknown` when the caller did not say. So an ABSENT field means the line was not written by v3+ code: it either predates v3, or the model hand-wrote it (the instruction to use workframe-event travels in the injected discipline shards; on Codex the SessionStart main shard additionally carries a `本会话 harness=codex session_id=…` line and the bin command falls back to the per-session marker file, so the instruction is DELIVERED to the Codex MAIN thread — observed by a zero-credential probe reading the rollout's context items. Narrower than it sounds: for sub-agent threads only the channel is verified (a review-type sub thread received the sub shard); full-shard arrival in `spawn_agent`-type sub threads has NOT been verified, and whether the model ACTS on the instruction on either thread type has not been observed — see __delivery_established__ for why the flag stays false). Consumers MUST keep the two apart — _harness.harness_breakdown() reports them as `unknown` vs `unstamped` — and MUST NOT re-default a v3-era `unknown` back to `cc`. Re-defaulting would silently misattribute a bin entry run from the Codex door, which is the exact failure this field exists to prevent; the cost of NOT re-defaulting is only that a CC-only project sees a small `unknown` bucket for manually run commands, which is a true statement rather than a lucky guess.

availability_values.__doc__: Per-event, per-harness producibility. Consumers MUST print a data-source line derived from this map before any cross-harness count, otherwise a structural absence reads as a real signal (e.g. 'Codex sessions fail less' when in fact turn_failed cannot be captured there). Computed, never hand-copied: _harness.events_by_availability() / _harness.harness_breakdown().
availability_values.full: Producer path exists on that harness with the same coverage as the other one.
availability_values.partial: At least one producer path is established on that door AND at least one is missing or not yet established. `note` MUST say which half and WHICH KIND — a known gap and an unjudged path are not the same claim, and collapsing them is the failure `unknown` was added to prevent.
availability_values.none: No producer path on that harness — absence of this event type there carries no information.
availability_values.unknown: No producer path is established on that door — nothing has been probed either way. Deliberately distinct from full: reporting an unverified path as available is the failure mode this value exists to prevent. Also distinct from partial, which requires at least one working path.
availability_values.note: Free text, REQUIRED whenever cc or codex is not full; it must name which emission path is affected and what the reader would otherwise mis-read.
availability_values.__how_to_judge__: GRADING RULE (explicit so the next author reproduces it; the first version of this map left it implicit and graded three SessionEnd-driven events too generously). Ask, per door, of EACH producer path: is that path ESTABLISHED on this door? WHAT A 'PATH' IS, since this bit is easy to get wrong: a path runs from the EMISSION POINT (the function that actually appends the event) out to the mounts that can REACH that function — not to every mount the enclosing script happens to have. One script can be mounted on several hooks and still have emission points reachable from only one of them: check-stale-modules.py sits on both SessionStart and PostToolUse, yet process_postool_use() is reachable only from the latter and clear_stale() only from a CLI subcommand. Grading at script granularity instead of emission-point granularity mis-grades exactly those. Then: none = no path can ever run here; unknown = NO path is established; partial = at least one path IS established AND at least one is missing-or-unestablished; full = every path is established. WHAT COUNTS AS ESTABLISHED: (a) a door-agnostic path — the model runs a CLI command or a script directly, no harness mechanism involved; or (b) a hook-mounted path whose hook event has been OBSERVED EXECUTING on that door by a probe AND — where the mount is MATCHER-SCOPED — whose matcher has been established on that door too. The matcher half is a separate layer and must be asked separately: a hook event can be observed executing while its matcher still never fires for the intended targets, because matchers name tool names and the two doors do not share a tool vocabulary. Today NO matcher-scoped mount is established on Codex: the Codex hook table carries the CC matchers verbatim (Bash / Edit|Write|NotebookEdit / Skill) and whether those tool names ever match on Codex has not been verified (it takes one credentialed tool call), so a path that reaches its producer only through a matcher-scoped mount is UNESTABLISHED there even though its hook event sits in the observed list. Skipping this layer is how the first version of this rule failed to reproduce three of its own entries. For Codex seven hook events have been observed executing: SessionStart, SubagentStart, PostToolUse, Stop (the first probe batch), UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd (the review-thread probe, then every zero-credential end-to-end run of the door — payloads captured), SubagentStop (the spawn_agent-type probe). The other five that the runtime enumerates (PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PreCompact, PostCompact, Interrupt) have NOT been observed running — PreToolUse was mounted in one probe but no tool call happened in a zero-credential run, so it stays unobserved; the other four were never mounted. A hook event merely APPEARING in that enumeration does NOT make it established: the enumeration was read out of the binary, not observed running. Grading by 'is the event name in the list' instead of 'has it been seen running' is exactly the mistake this paragraph exists to stop. WHAT COUNTS AS DISPROVEN (this is what separates `none` from `unknown`, and the first version of this rule could not express it): a path is IMPOSSIBLE, not merely unestablished, in either of two ways. (i) THE MECHANISM IS ABSENT: the hook event name does not appear in that runtime's event enumeration at all, so no probe could ever see it fire. (ii) A PROBE RAN AND THE EVENT DID NOT COME: the mechanism exists and was exercised, and the trace was measured absent — this is a positive finding, not a missing measurement. `skill_invoked` is `none` on Codex through BOTH: UserPromptExpansion is absent by (i), and PostToolUse with the Skill matcher was exercised and produced no trace by (ii). When leaning on (ii), the `note` MUST carry the probe's scope verbatim — an entry path that was not exercised is not disproven, it is unknown, and blurring the two turns a bounded measurement into an unbounded claim. `turn_failed` and `config_changed` are `none` on Codex for that reason (StopFailure / ConfigChange are not among its events), whereas `signoff_guard_error` is only `unknown` (PostToolUse IS observed running, but both of its mounts are matcher-scoped and the matcher half is unverified). Both read as 'no established path', so grading on observation alone collapses them; ask whether the mechanism EXISTS before asking whether it has been SEEN. `session_ended` is the worked example of an entry that moved: it sat at `unknown` while SessionEnd was merely enumerated, and became `full` once SessionEnd was observed running on that door. MODEL-SIDE EVENTS (protocol_expected / model_mediated) are graded full on both doors because the write itself is door-agnostic — a model with shell and file access performs it identically. DECLARED CAVEAT, not an oversight: what is NOT yet established is whether the INSTRUCTION to write reaches the model on the Codex door (skill / rule / context delivery). Those events are therefore full-but-conditional; a reader seeing zero of them on Codex should suspect delivery before suspecting the model. This axis is deliberately not folded into the grade — folding it in would merge 'the mechanism may not exist' with 'the mechanism exists but is not wired yet', and only the first is a risk to the reader.

__delivery_established__.__doc__: Per door: is the chain that TELLS the model to write an event established there? Model-side events (protocol_expected / model_mediated) are graded `full` because the write itself is door-agnostic, but a reader still needs to know that zero of them on a door may mean 'never asked' rather than 'never happened'. This flag is what _harness.harness_breakdown() computes the full_but_delivery_unverified table from; flip a door to true when its skill / rule / context delivery lands and the table empties itself. WHAT 'LANDS' MEANS FOR codex, so the flip is not made on partial evidence: the instruction (use the workframe-event bin command) travels in the injected discipline shards; the main-thread shard has been observed arriving in a Codex rollout, and a review-type sub thread has been observed receiving the sub shard — that is the CHANNEL. It stays false until BOTH remaining halves are observed: (i) full-shard arrival in a `spawn_agent`-type sub thread (only the channel is verified there, not the whole shard), and (ii) a model on that door actually writing an event through the bin command after reading the shard. Flipping on channel evidence alone would turn 'never asked' into 'never happened' for exactly the reader this flag protects. Keep it a flag, not prose: a hand-written caveat in a report template is a copy, and copies drift — which is the one thing this whole section forbids.

availability.note: 模型手写，两门皆可。harness 字段由 `workframe-event` 打上：告知模型用它的指令随注入的纪律片投递，Codex 门主线程实测抵达（main 片首行带 `本会话 harness=codex session_id=…`，bin 命令另有会话标记文件兜底）；**模型是否照做未观察、`spawn_agent` 型子线程全片抵达未验**——所以 `__delivery_established__.codex` 仍是 false，该门下这类事件为零时先怀疑投递、再怀疑模型。没有 harness 字段的行是 v3 之前写的，按缺省读作 cc。

skill_used.producer: agent wrap-up protocol (the event-stream step of the injected common protocol shard, executed by the model)

fields.success: boolean, required (true=delivered promised artifact / false=did not deliver, user rejected, blocked exit, voluntary abort)
fields.session_id: string, optional but strongly recommended — used by check-iteration-trigger.py to enforce per-session activity cap (3.0 per session). Source: $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID env var (injected into Bash subprocesses since CC 2.1.132, same value as hooks' stdin session_id) when available, else omit (script falls back to ts which silently disables the cap). Note: $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID (without CODE) was never a Bash env var — it is the SKILL.md content substitution syntax.
fields.cli_available: boolean, optional — obsidian-* skills: whether the Obsidian CLI was usable
fields.fallback_used: boolean, optional — obsidian-* skills: whether it degraded to Read/rg
fields.operation: string, optional — obsidian-* / doc-graph-health: sub-operation name

skill_used.caveats: Counts may be slightly off if a subagent skips wrap-up. (The older 'preloaded but unused skill' caveat no longer applies: agent frontmatter preloading is retired, and a skill merely named in the SubagentStart point-name section produces no skill_used event unless it is actually invoked.) Corroborate with rollback_applied / proposal_applied for high-confidence skill activity. Without session_id, per-session cap silently devolves into per-event cap. The four optional extension fields are written by the obsidian-* skills and doc-graph-health; consumers must tolerate their absence and must not reject events that carry them.

availability.note: 同 skill_used：模型手写，两门皆可；harness 由 `workframe-event` 打上，指令随纪律片投递、Codex 主线程实测抵达，模型是否照做未观察（`__delivery_established__.codex` 仍 false）。

user_correction.producer: the correction-detection flow (judgement half in the injected main shard, procedure half in skill signal-intake) writes immediately when it writes the [纠正] entry (role/shared MEMORY, or auto-memory when scope=main per 两套记忆分工契约); agent wrap-up must not emit a duplicate user_correction for the same correction

fields.scope: shared | <role> | main (main = 主 Claude 层纠正，落 auto-memory，无 sidecar)
fields.role: agent role string (if scope != shared); omitted when scope=main
fields.entry_key: string (memory-index sidecar key for the protected [纠正] entry); omitted when scope=main (auto-memory has no sidecar) and when the correction lands in a skill/rule file instead of MEMORY (sidecar only indexes MEMORY entries; put the target file path in summary)
fields.summary: short snapshot of the corrected fact, required so memory-log does not depend on current sidecar state

user_correction.caveats: Depends on the model recognizing the correction signal AND following the correction handling in the injected main-session signal-intake shard. Misses possible if the agent silently incorporates the correction without ceremony.

availability.note: 同 skill_used：模型手写，两门皆可；harness 由 `workframe-event` 打上，指令随纪律片投递、Codex 主线程实测抵达，模型是否照做未观察（`__delivery_established__.codex` 仍 false）。

task_blocked.producer: Primary producer = test-case-design skill (QA-driven flow: test failure → SEC/BUG issue → status=blocked → skill appends event). Fallback producer = current agent wrap-up (the event-stream step of the injected common protocol shard), restricted to non-QA / manual blocked transitions that did NOT go through test-case-design; fallback MUST dedup-check the FULL events.jsonl for the same task_id before appending (task_id-only scope — this schema has no session_id field, so session-scoped dedup is not machine-executable; full-history is a conservative approximation that may skip a repeated manual re-block of the same task, accepted trade-off, see the task_blocked fallback dedup rule in the injected common protocol shard).
task_blocked.caveats: Producer policy is primary+fallback (NOT sole producer) — see the task_blocked producer policy in the injected common protocol shard (§Step 1 — 事件流). Without dedup, both test-case-design and wrap-up would append for the same QA-driven blocked transition, double-counting the 2.0 problem weight. Do NOT revert producer wording to 'qa agent wrap-up' alone (qa wrap-up alone misses skill-driven appends) nor to 'sole producer = test-case-design' (which contradicts the fallback path for non-QA / manual blocked transitions). Starvation record (2026-08 audit, G1#3): zero occurrences in 3+ months of consumer-project events — diagnosed as architectural starvation, NOT producer breakage (project QA loop idle; board history has zero blocked tasks). Mechanism and weight retained as-is; consumer pipeline verified by synthetic drill 2026-08-06. Doctor labels count==0 + producer-text-present as 'never-triggered (starved)', distinct from missing-producer 'broken promise'.

availability.note: 唯一 producer 是 session-end-flush.py，只挂 `SessionEnd` 一处，**没有任何门无关的旁路**。`SessionEnd` 在 Codex 侧**已被观察到执行**：早期探针的 marker 计数（`codex exec` 一次 +1；review 型子线程上只在父线程触发一次）、装机器零凭据验活会话里本事件以 `harness: codex` 落盘（`workframe-door --check --live` 把它列为五条无条件侧效应之一）。无 matcher、无第二条路径 ⇒ `full`。**边界**：只在 `codex exec` 与 review 型两条路径上观察过；app-server 客户端直接杀线程（无 SessionEnd）时本事件缺席是客户端行为，不是本门的结构缺口。

fields.reason: clear | resume | logout | prompt_input_exit | bypass_permissions_disabled | other — stdin 解析失败时回退 other（不得自造 unknown 等枚举外值）

session_ended.caveats: Will NOT fire if Claude Code is forcibly terminated (window closed, SIGKILL, OS shutdown). For those cases the next SessionStart's drift check serves as the recovery signal.

availability.note: 两条 producer 路径：① `recompute_board_summary.py` 经 bin 命令由模型 / 用户直跑，**门无关、已确立**；② `session-end-flush.py` 在 `SessionEnd` 上自动重算——`SessionEnd` 在 Codex 侧已被观察到执行（见 `session_ended`），且本事件本身在装机器零凭据验活会话里以 `harness: codex` 落盘。两条都确立 ⇒ `full`。

skill_metrics_recomputed.purpose: Deterministic refresh marker for .workframe/state/skill-metrics.yaml. The file is derived from events.jsonl and can be regenerated.

fields.drift_fields: object mapping field name to {summary, actual} pair (e.g., {pending: {summary: 5, actual: 7}})
fields.repair_status: ok | skipped | error (status returned from recompute call)
fields.likely_cause: string (e.g., 'SessionEnd hook skipped or timed out in previous session')

summary_drift_repaired.purpose: C+ drift check 自动修复事件——SessionStart 检测到 summary vs tasks 不一致时触发；让 audit 能追溯 drift 频率，间接判断 SessionEnd 是否经常超时

fields.reason: unknown_statuses_in_tasks | tasks_unparsed | summary_block_not_found | recompute_failed | recompute_skipped | read_failed | import_failed | parse_failed — 裸枚举值，不拼接详情
fields.detail: string, optional — 异常类型与消息（截断 100 字）；reason=recompute_skipped 时放 recompute 自己返回的 reason（本文件的 reason 只用自己那套词表，recompute 加新 reason 不必回改此处）。详情放这里，保证 reason 可被等值匹配的消费方命中
fields.repair_status: ok | skipped | error（recompute 实际返回的 status；reason=recompute_skipped 时恒为 skipped，与 summary_drift_repaired 的同名字段同义）
fields.unknown_statuses: list of unknown status values (only when reason=unknown_statuses_in_tasks)
fields.drift_fields: object mapping field name to {summary, actual} pair (when applicable)

summary_drift_repair_skipped.purpose: C+ 第一保护条件——drift check 发现 tasks 含未知 status（如 'completd' 拼写错误）时不自动修复，让用户自己检查；audit 会展示这条事件提示用户处理

pending_maintenance_dismissed.producer: All four callers now write through code — maintenance_workorder.py: `--commit` (manifest close_pm) and `--close-pm <PM-ID>... [--reason <text>]` (invoked by maintenance-review mode A, self-iteration when closing trigger entries with reason=self_iteration_no_proposal, and librarian after clearing a memory_backlog). Before 2026-08-16 the latter three told the model to hand-edit activity-state.json, which bypassed the file lock / atomic replace / three-way merge; the tier stays model_mediated (the WEAKEST link) because whether the model remembers to RUN the command is still model-dependent — but once run, the write itself is code-guaranteed.

fields.reason: string, optional — free-form closure reason, passed through by `--close-pm ... --reason <text>`; self-iteration writes the fixed token self_iteration_no_proposal, the other paths usually omit it. NOT an enum: the only consumer (audit) prints it in the dismissal trail, it is never aggregated by value. availability.note: 两个入口在 Codex 侧都不可得：UserPromptExpansion 无对等 hook 事件；PostToolUse(Skill) 侧已实测**不产生留痕**。**作用域必须照抄，不许读宽**：实测证的是「skill 作为 spawn_agent 的上下文项进入子 agent 时不产生 PostToolUse」（SKILL.md 全文以 role:user 消息到达，不是 function_call；同批 9 次 PostToolUse 的 tool_name 无一含 skill，而同一过滤器对 agent 得 6、对 mcp 得 3，证明它能算出非零）。**主 agent 在自己轮次里用 $skill 直调那条路径仍未测**——这里的 none 只覆盖已实测的那条入口，不代表已穷尽所有入口。

skill_invoked.producer: scripts/log-skill-invoked.py, wired to two entries: UserPromptExpansion (user types /skill-name; the command expands into a prompt WITHOUT going through the Skill tool) and PostToolUse matcher:Skill (model invokes the Skill tool). The first entry is the important one — direct slash-command typing is the most common way skills get used. Field extraction is multi-candidate by design (command / command_name / prompt / user_prompt / expanded_prompt): CC makes no hard promise about the UserPromptExpansion stdin schema, and betting on a single key means this entry fails 100% silently if the key is named differently — no events at all, while every consumer concludes 'nobody uses skills'.
consumers: workframe_doctor.py check_events_parse (近 30 天调起数，与 skill_used 并列展示、不相加)
audit (可读；当前 SKILL 输出模板未单列该行，展示与否由该 skill 自行决定)
skill_invoked.relationship_to_skill_used: COEXIST, NEVER SUM. skill_invoked answers 'was it invoked' (code-guaranteed); skill_used answers 'was it used and did it deliver' (model-written, carries the success self-assessment). One invocation produces both — adding them double-counts.

fields.skill: bare skill name — plugin prefix stripped (`/core:module-init` -> `module-init`), leading slash stripped, first token only. MUST stay in the same namespace as `skill_used.skill` (which agent wrap-up writes bare): if one side keeps the `core:` prefix, any consumer aggregating by skill name counts one skill as two. Event is skipped entirely when the value does not look like a skill name — better no record than a flood of prompt text masquerading as skill names.
fields.entry: command_expansion | skill_tool — which of the two entries fired
fields.session_id: from hook stdin, omitted when unavailable
fields.agent_type: present only when fired inside a subagent (pending spike verification)
fields.plugin: optional — the stripped plugin prefix (e.g. `core`), present only when the invocation carried one. Kept as a separate field so `skill` stays comparable with skill_used.
